content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text resolves a collision between the defender's and challenger's chains over Acts 2:30, so it is the kind of chain-against-chain assessment K-C governs.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"weighs chain against chain by footing — I weighed whether the judge's 'neither chain forces the other' is a chain-against-chain comparison by footing or a failure to identify footing.","why":"The judge compares the defender's and challenger's chains as wholes and labels the collision underdetermined, without applying the retired stating-verse test, so it complies with K-C."}
